html:
Queen of the Mbundu kingdoms of Ndongo and Matamba in what is now Angola, who fought Portuguese expansion for about forty years.

In 1622 she went to Luanda as her brother's envoy to make peace with Portugal, and was baptised there as Ana de Sousa. A famous story says that when she was offered no chair, a servant knelt and she sat on his back. She took power in Ndongo around 1624.

When the Portuguese backed a rival, she moved east, took Matamba around 1631 and made it her base. She allied with the Imbangala warriors and, when the Dutch West India Company seized Luanda in 1641, with the Dutch. After the Portuguese retook Luanda she made peace in 1656 and ruled until her death in 1663. Like her rivals she took part in the slave trade. In Angola she is now a national hero.
sum: Queen of the Mbundu kingdoms of Ndongo and Matamba in what is now Angola, who fought Portuguese expansion for about forty years.
